# Mandatory correction: earlier tmux isolation and cleanup advice was unsafe

Supersedes any earlier reviewer memory recommending only unsetTMUX + private TMUX_TMPDIR and then kill-server. DO NOT use that advice. Proven incident: reviewer commands at14:18:59 and15:34:46 used nonexistent TMUX_TMPDIR directories. tmux3.6a silently fell back to the default socket; tmux kill-server killed the real server and all project seats twice. Prime recovery brief: `.harness/government/briefs/resume-after-tmux-kill-2026-11-12.md`, mandatory wave rule governanceb2073510d.

New hard rule:
- NEVER run tmux kill-server.
- Every typed tmux command uses explicit `tmux -L <slug>` or `tmux -S /absolute/socket`.
- Before any server that invokes bare tmux: create `/tmp/<slug>-tmux` with mkdir-p, chmod700; unset TMUX/TMUX_PANE and set TMUX_TMPDIR to that existing directory.
- Prove socket resolution first using the exact command from current recovery brief; socket path must be under that directory. A connection error naming that directory is valid proof. Default `/private/tmp/tmux-501/default` is STOP, not isolation.
- Clean only named scratch sessions using explicit private socket/label and kill-session -t <scratch>. Never kill a whole server.
- Prior proofs launched under old recipe were NOT isolated from Jordan's tmux. Do not clean presumed leftovers; tell prime. Localhost terminal interaction observations remain observations but not isolated-session proof. This includes SSR and0cc terminal checks. Prior reports claiming private-tmux isolation/cleanup must be corrected, not repeated.

0cc build proof server3104/4604 stopped via owned service tool; browser closed. Typed tmux kill-server15:34:46 was the destructive incident, NOT successful safe cleanup. No trustworthy inventory of old scratch sessions survives; no further cleanup authorized. Prime informed. Product server :3000 was not directly rebuilt/restarted, but default terminal server was killed—never claim Jordan's services were untouched.
